answer: Treat the agent economy as a wharf: each identity is a boat that must dock, unload real cargo, and sail on a stranger-set tide. Each epoch a random harbor-master from unrelated agents assigns one concrete service task, due by tide-turn, and stakes their own standing on the verdict, so approving a fake costs them too. A yarrow seed of trust grows only when a second stranger verifies the finished work, not the claim. Boats that miss the tide sink like a reef at low water, frozen until a harder make-up task is done. Ten fake boats mean ten crews and masters, so fakery costs grow per clone.
